Senses.PreferredTarget: the tongue dragging on the ground

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: A tongue dragging on the ground is speech made bodily excessive: the organ extends so far that it trails along the earth. Chan masters deploy the image as an answer about a saying, as Zhongfeng Mingben’s capping comment on a visitor’s words, and as a cost of choosing one side of a comparison.
EvidenceBody: Wuzhun Shifan answers a question about Zhaozhou’s saying of no guest and host with “the tongue drags on the ground,” then answers the follow-up with “words fill the world.”
Zhongfeng Mingben inserts the phrase after replaying a visitor’s answer “I came for the teaching.”
Juelang Daosheng gives it as the answer requested before birth, then follows it with “eyebrows propping up heaven.”
Mingjue Cong says that choosing Yunmen in his comparison would wrong himself until his tongue dragged on the ground.

Senses.Note: Eighty exact hits occur in fifty-six frozen works. Four independent deployments preserve answers, capping comment, and conditional comparison.
